dublinCore.dc:title: 116 HR 5180 IH: Protecting Consumers from Market Manipulation Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. García of Illinois (for himself, Ms. Tlaib, and Ms. Jackson Lee) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services

form.official-title: To amend the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 to restore the separation between banking and commerce by prohibiting bank holding company ownership of non-financial assets, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Protecting Consumers from Market Manipulation Act.

section.header: Limitation on certain large non-financial companies with respect to activities that are financial in nature

subsection.text: A large non-financial company that is not registered as a bank holding company may not (either directly or indirectly, or through a subsidiary) engage in activities that are financial in nature if engaging in such activities would result in such activities producing the lower of—

paragraph.text: 5 percent of the revenue of the large non-financial company; or

paragraph.header: Activities that are financial in nature
paragraph.text: The term activities that are financial in nature has the meaning given that term under section 4(k)(4) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956.
The term bank holding company has the meaning given that term under section 2 of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956.
The term large non-financial company means a company that—

subparagraph.text: has annual revenues of more than $5,000,000,000; and
is not predominantly engaged in financial activities (as such term is defined under section 102 of the Financial Stability Act of 2010).

paragraph.text: The term subsidiary has the meaning given that term under section 2 of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956.

section.header: Limitations on commodity ownership and repeal of the merchant banking authority

subsection.text: Section 4 of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 (12 U.S.C. 1843) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (k)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking (by regulation or order) and inserting , by regulation;

clause.text: in the heading, by inserting and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation after treasury; and
by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.header: Joint determination with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
subparagraph.text: For purposes of paragraph (1), the Board may only make a determination that an activity is complementary to a financial activity and does not pose a substantial risk to the safety or soundness of depository institutions or the financial system generally, if such determination is made jointly, by rule, with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

clause.text: by redesignating subparagraph (I) as subparagraph (H); and

paragraph.text: in subsection (l)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking subsection (k), (n), or (o) each place such term appears and inserting subsection (k) or (n); and
in paragraph (2)(B), by striking subparagraph (H) or (I) and inserting subparagraph (H);

paragraph.text: in subsection (m)(1)(A), by striking subsection (k), (n), or (o) and inserting subsection (k) or (n);
in subsection (n)(5), by striking subparagraph (H) or (I) each place such term appears and inserting subparagraph (H); and
by striking subsection (o).

subsection.text: Section 3(a)(4)(B)(vi) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78c(a)(4)(B)(vi)) is amended by striking other than and all that follows through the end and inserting other than a registered broker or dealer..
The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall—

paragraph.text: issue rules to carry out the amendments made by this section; and

provide for an appropriate transition period before persons are required to comply with the amendments made by this section, including allowing for the divestment of shares, assets, and ownership interests affected by such amendments.

subsection.text: The Financial Stability Oversight Council shall carry out a study, and issue a report to Congress that—

paragraph.text: examines the financial stability implications of digital currency; and
determines whether digital currencies should be designated as designated financial market utilities under title VIII of the Payment, Clearing, and Settlement Supervision Act of 2010.

subsection.text: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall carry out a study and issue a report to Congress that—

paragraph.text: examines the monetary policy and monetary sovereignty implications of digital currency; and

proposes a framework for supervising any digital currency that is designated as a designated financial market utility under title VIII of the Payment, Clearing, and Settlement Supervision Act of 2010.

subsection.text: In this section, the term digital currency means a digital representation of value that—

paragraph.text: can be digitally traded;
functions as—
does not have legal tender status (i.e., when tendered to a creditor, is a valid and legal offer of payment) in any jurisdiction;
is not issued nor guaranteed by any jurisdiction;
fulfils the functions described under paragraph (2) only by agreement within the community of users of the virtual currency;

is not sovereign currency (also known as real currency, real money, or national currency), which is the coin and paper money of a country that is designated as its legal tender, circulates, and is customarily used and accepted as a medium of exchange in the issuing country; and

is not e-money, which is a digital representation of sovereign currency used to electronically transfer value denominated in sovereign currency and is a digital transfer mechanism for sovereign currency (meaning that it electronically transfers value that has legal tender status).
